Independent proof reconstruction and bounded binary reproduction
correctness.rationale: For the free class-two Lie algebra with three generators, every automorphism is determined by its invertible quotient map g and an arbitrary central shear f; its central block is the exterior square of g. Restriction and projection of f onto the map from ker(g-I) to coker(exterior-square(g)-I) are surjective, giving q^(9-ac) lifts per map and fixed dimension a+c-t for rank t. Exterior duality identifies c with the eigenspace dimension at det(g). At fixed determinant, prescribing a scalar action on a line or plane leaves respectively q^2|SL_2(q)| or q^2 block choices. The only exceptional nonunit determinant (meaning determinant different from 1) for a scalar block contributing c=3 is -1 in odd characteristic. For determinant different from 1, coexistence of the two eigenvalues forces a double eigenvalue 1 and simple eigenvalue det(g); the split and Jordan cases have the two class sizes in the proof. This verifies the joint table and its rank refinement. An irreducible cubic block, a regular unipotent block, and the identity with shears realize respectively dimension 0, dimensions 1 and 2, and dimensions 3 through 6. Burnside normalization follows from the three element orbits. A fresh direct binary check enumerating all 86,016 six-dimensional automorphisms by minors and bitwise rank reproduced (24576,25088,29120,6216,966,49,1). Replay: python /tmp/opencode/frozen_review_reproduce.py fixedspace.
residual_risks: The reproduction is binary; general q follows from the eigenspace and shear enumeration, not from extrapolation.

value.rationale: Rank three is the first free two-step case in which the exterior-square block has the same dimension as the generating space but can have a different fixed-space dimension. The full distribution, including the characteristic-dependent scalar stratum and the change in fixed dimension caused by shears, provides an exact baseline for fixed-vector statistics beyond a mere orbit average or single exceptional count.
residual_risks: No implication is established for higher ranks, arbitrary quotients, or automorphisms of the underlying finite group.
